tool_input.command: bun run typecheck 2>&1 | tail -5; git stash -q && bun test 2>&1 | tail -4; git stash pop -q
tool_input.description: Typecheck and confirm baseline test noise

result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` pass (12 tests, 0 failures; the 422 log line in the output is pre-existing noise from the starter `posts.search` test).

I made the excerpt optional end-to-end and added a body-derived fallback. In `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` the `excerpt` field on `PostPayloadSchema` dropped its `min(1)` and became `.optional()` (still trimmed, still capped at 500), so a missing, empty, or whitespace-only excerpt validates while a blank title or body is still a 422. The derivation rule lives as a new static `Post.excerptFrom(body)` in `app/Models/Post.ts`: it trims the body, returns it unchanged when it is 140 characters or fewer, and otherwise keeps the first 140 characters — pulling back to the last whitespace only when the cut would split a word (both character 140 and 141 non-whitespace) and staying at 140 when the opening has no whitespace at all — then trims trailing whitespace and appends a single `…`. `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts` gained a small `withExcerpt()` helper applied in both `store()` and `update()`, so a provided excerpt wins as typed and a blank one is re-derived from the (new) body on every save. The New/Edit forms (`resources/js/pages/posts/New.tsx`, `Edit.tsx`) now label the field "Excerpt (optional)" with a placeholder explaining the fallback and tolerate an undefined value; `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` was regenerated via `bun run codegen` so the body type reads `excerpt?: string`. New tests in `tests/PostExcerpt.test.ts` cover the derivation (including both worked examples, the 140-character boundary, and the no-whitespace case) and the relaxed schema.
